title: How To Ensure Students Wear Masks And Socially Distance ocially-distance/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Anticipating a return to in-person school under mask and social-distancing mandates, Linsin predicts that most students will take the protocols seriously once they physically encounter hand-washing stations, plexiglass barriers, and directional markings, and recommends teachers spend the first week simply observing rather than immediately imposing new rules. However, he specifies a fallback: if compliance starts slipping among students or colleagues, teachers should add two explicit new rules to their classroom management plan — keep the mask on and covering the nose and mouth, and maintain six feet of distance — taught and modeled with the same precision as any other classroom rule. He frames the goal as protecting the teacher's own peace of mind and the school from liability, not making a political statement about the pandemic itself, and stresses that any new rule is meaningless unless enforced with total consistency.
points: Spend the first week back simply observing whether mask and distancing protocols are being followed naturally.
If compliance slips, add two explicit new rules to your classroom management plan: mask coverage and six-foot distancing.
Teach and model any new Covid rule with the same precision and clarity used for existing classroom rules.
Enforce new rules with total consistency, or they will carry no real weight.
Treat this as protecting your own peace of mind and the school from liability, independent of any political debate.
quotes: The likelihood, however, is that masks and social distancing will be the policy whenever you go back to school.

I think upon entering campus again for the first time—with its hand-washing stations, directional markings, plexiglass barriers, and regimented movements—students will realize the seriousness of what they’re about to undertake.
My recommendation then during the first week back to school is to just observe.
Keep your mask on and covering your nose and mouth at all times unless given permission to remove it.
Making it part of your classroom management plan is the only effective way to ensure masks are worn and social distancing is maintained.
Grab hold of your peace of mind and hang onto it for all it’s worth.
